text: This chapter introduces 3-part 4ths (quartal harmony), a voicing system derived from stacked 4ths that stands in exact opposition to tertial (3rd-based) triads. The core pedagogical challenge is the diminished 4th enharmonic problem — the interval between B and Eb sounds like a major 3rd despite appearing as a 4th on the staff — which can cause quartal voicings to collapse into triadic sonorities and fail in quartal context. The chapter establishes interval taxonomy showing that 4th voicings prioritize 4ths and 5ths while excluding 3rds and 6ths (the inverse of triads), and introduces a guitar-specific drop-D pedal technique using the low D string as a harmonic anchor to safely explore 4th-voicing cycles in D Dorian mode, where the absence of avoid notes enables free exploration. The chapter extends these harmonic tools into melodic generation through arpeggiation, encouraging students to discover melodies hidden within 4th voicing shapes.
